patches.value: From M003 and the exact M008 formula, for each positive scale r_j tending to zero choose a Nat-indexed cover (U_{j,i}) of E with ediam(U_{j,i})≤r_j and total q-cost <γ_j, where γ_j>0 tends to zero. Replace each zero-diameter singleton by a ball of diameter ≤r_j and added q-cost with sum <γ_j. This witness follows from the M003 zero-measure result and M008 cover infimum, not compactness alone.

For a>0 and δ>0, C_a(A,δ) is the ENNReal infimum of ∑'_{i:ℕ} ediam(U_i)^a over all Nat-indexed sequences of subsets of the ambient metric space satisfying A⊆⋃_i U_i and ediam(U_i)≤δ for every i. Empty and zero-diameter members are allowed and cost zero since 0^a=0. Finite covers are represented by appending empty members. This is exactly the scale content from M008.

Let D=dim_H(E), F=E×[0,1]. First show 0≤D≤n<∞. Nonnegativity is part of the critical-exponent definition. If n=0, ℝ⁰ is a singleton and E is that singleton, so D=0. If n>0, compactness H002 implies boundedness, so E lies in a bounded box. For every sufficiently small h>0, subdivide the box into at most C h^(−n) grid cubes, C independent of h, each of diameter ≤√n h. For fixed m>n their total m-power diameter cost is at most C n^(m/2)h^(m−n)→0. These covers at scales tending to zero give H^m(E)=0 from M008, hence D≤n. Fix arbitrary q>D; q>0. M003 at the NNReal coercion of q gives H^q(E)=0. Unfold M008: this is the supremum over positive scales of the infimum cover cost, so every scale content C_q(E,r)=0. For every r>0 and γ>0, the infimum definition therefore supplies a Nat-indexed r-cover of cost <γ (admissible covers exist, e.g. a singleton cover). Choose r_j↓0, r_j≤1, and γ_j↓0 with covers of cost <γ_j. Each nonempty zero-diameter member in Euclidean space is a singleton. Enumerate these members by a finite or countable list and replace the k-th by an open ball containing it, of diameter ≤r_j and q-power cost <γ_j2^(−k−1); total added cost is <γ_j. Leave positive-diameter members and empty members unchanged. The resulting cover has all nonempty diameters d_i positive, d_i≤r_j, and q-cost <2γ_j. Partition [0,1] for each i into at most ⌈1/d_i⌉+1≤2/d_i closed intervals of length ≤d_i. Products U_i×K_iℓ cover F, have diameter ≤√2d_i, and form a countable family (countable union of finite families), which can be enumerated by ℕ with empty members appended. Their total (q+1)-cost is at most 2(√2)^(q+1)∑d_i^q<4(√2)^(q+1)γ_j, tending to zero, and their diameters are ≤√2r_j→0. M008 gives H^(q+1)(F)=0; M012 at NNReal exponent q+1 gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. Since this holds for all q>D, density gives dim_H(F)≤D+1. For n=0, F is isometric to [0,1]; interval covers of mesh tending to zero have total a-cost tending to zero for each a>1, so H^a(F)=0 and M012 gives dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Isometries preserve ediam, cover conditions, and the exact M008 formula.
Instantiate with α=ℝ with its Borel measurable space, β=ℕ, μ=ν=volume.restrict([0,1]), and f(i,t)=ρ_i^s·1_{J_i∩[0,1]}(t).
ℕ is countable. Each J_i∩[0,1] is Borel in ℝ, so its indicator is measurable; multiplication by constant ρ_i^s preserves measurability and hence gives AEMeasurability for ν.
Use the pointwise slicing inequality on [0,1], multiplied on all of ℝ by 1_[0,1], and integrate with ν=volume.restrict([0,1]); ν is supported on [0,1], so this is the same ν-a.e. inequality.
J_i∩[0,1] is Borel in ℝ, therefore measurable for the ambient Borel space and eligible in M010 with restricted measure ν and ENNReal constant ρ_i^s.

value.bindings: Use endpoints a_i≤b_i of a closed interval containing J_i∩[0,1], with b_i−a_i≤ρ_i+η_i.
hypothesis_checks: M011 has no additional hypotheses; it gives volume([a_i,b_i])=ofReal(b_i−a_i) for arbitrary real endpoints.

patches.value: Instantiate measure_mono for Lebesgue volume, with measurable set J_i∩[0,1] contained in the enclosing closed interval [a_i,b_i].
The interval enclosure gives J_i∩[0,1]⊆[a_i,b_i]; Lebesgue volume, as a measure, is an outer measure.

For D>0 fix 0<s<D. For a>0 define C_a(A,δ)=inf{∑'ᵢ ediam(Uᵢ)^a : U:ℕ→Set(X), A⊆⋃ᵢUᵢ and ∀i ediam(Uᵢ)≤δ}. Empty members have diameter zero and hence zero cost. In M008, the supremum over nonempty witnesses is the ordinary power for a nonempty member and zero for the empty member; thus its inner infimum is exactly this content and H^a(A)=sup_{δ>0}C_a(A,δ), with no normalization factor. If δ₁≤δ₂, every δ₁-admissible cover is δ₂-admissible, so C_a(A,δ₁)≥C_a(A,δ₂). The one-sided limit as scale decreases to zero therefore equals this supremum. M001 gives H^s(E)=∞; hence C_s(E,δ)→∞, meaning that for every finite K all sufficiently small positive δ have C_s(E,δ)>K. Fix δ>0 and any countable δ-cover (Vᵢ) of F. Set ρᵢ=ediam(Vᵢ), Aᵢ=π₁(Vᵢ), Bᵢ=π₂(Vᵢ). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz in the concatenated Euclidean metric, so diam(Aᵢ),diam(Bᵢ)≤ρᵢ≤δ. Given ε>0 set ηᵢ=ε2^(−i−1)/(1+ρᵢ^s)>0. Each Bᵢ is bounded; extending the interval between its infimum and supremum by total width ηᵢ gives an open interval Jᵢ⊇Bᵢ of length ≤ρᵢ+ηᵢ. For every t∈[0,1] and x∈E, (x,t) lies in some Vᵢ, so x∈Aᵢ and t∈Bᵢ⊆Jᵢ. Therefore the Aᵢ with t∈Jᵢ cover E at scale δ. The definition of infimum gives C_s(E,δ)≤∑'ᵢ1_{Jᵢ∩[0,1]}(t)ρᵢ^s pointwise for t∈[0,1]. Put ν=volume.restrict([0,1]) on ambient Borel ℝ. For integration on all ℝ multiply the left side by 1_[0,1]; outside [0,1] it is zero, and ν is supported on [0,1], so the resulting inequality holds ν-a.e. Every Jᵢ∩[0,1] is Borel; its indicator multiplied by ρᵢ^s is measurable and AEMeasurable for ν. The ambient total mass is ν(ℝ)=volume([0,1])=ofReal(1−0)=1 by the restriction definition and M011; thus ν is finite and ν([0,1])=1. Integrate by M009 and use M002 to interchange the ℕ-indexed sum and lintegral; countability and AEMeasurability have just been checked. By M010 each summand integral equals ρᵢ^sν(Jᵢ∩[0,1]). If S=Jᵢ∩[0,1], then ν(S)=volume(S∩[0,1])=volume(S). Choose [aᵢ,bᵢ] containing S, with aᵢ≤bᵢ and bᵢ−aᵢ≤ρᵢ+ηᵢ. M013 gives volume(S)≤volume([aᵢ,bᵢ]), and M011 evaluates this as ofReal(bᵢ−aᵢ)≤ofReal(ρᵢ+ηᵢ). Thus C_s(E,δ)≤∑'ᵢρᵢ^(s+1)+∑'ᵢηᵢρᵢ^s≤∑'ᵢρᵢ^(s+1)+ε because ηᵢρᵢ^s≤ε2^(−i−1) and ∑ᵢ2^(−i−1)=1. For the fixed cover, ε is arbitrary: if its (s+1)-cost is finite, ε↓0 gives C_s(E,δ)≤that cost; if infinite the inequality is immediate. Taking the infimum over all covers gives C_s(E,δ)≤C_(s+1)(F,δ). As δ decreases to zero the left side diverges, so the right side diverges; M008 gives H^(s+1)(F)=∞. Apply M001 with NNReal exponent s+1 to obtain s+1≤dim_H(F). This holds for every 0<s<D, so density implies D+1≤dim_H(F). Use NNReal coercions for dimension theorems and the corresponding real exponents in M008.
